title: NDH payer endpoint and organization coverage
headline: The 2026-10-07 release names 997 payer organizations and 7,575 health plans, and 0 of those organizations carry an endpoint. At least 194 of 111,259 FHIR REST endpoints are payer provider-directory addresses (50 by URL path and 144 only by host), none of them attached to a payer organization; the Capital BlueCross control directory URL is not in the index, though another Capital BlueCross directory address is.
notes:
Re-measured against the 2026-10-07 release by streaming the published NDJSON directly, not through BigQuery. Classification rules are imported from analysis/payer_directory.py rather than copied, so this cannot drift from the finding it updates. 997 organizations carry the payer type (pay); 0 of them carry an endpoint and 0 a telecom entry, so no payer directory can be found from the payer organization record itself.

A FHIR REST address counts as a payer provider directory on either of two signals. Path: the URL names a directory (providerdirectory, provider-directory, plan-net, pdex). Host: the address sits on a host that serves a payer's directory, shown either by a CMS contract ID that the release's own InsurancePlan resources carry (962 contract IDs, found on 26 hosts), or by a hand-checked list of payer directory hosts. Of the 194: 25 path only, 144 host only, 25 both. By URL shape, 138 are CMS Medicare Advantage bulk directory files (MPF index.json and similar), 50 are FHIR API base addresses, and 6 are template addresses submitted with the placeholder unfilled (such as ppp-cccc-nnn), counted but in neither group. 9 sit on hosts named as QA or UAT. A host signal never overrides a path that marks a patient-access, authorization, member or other non-directory API, and shared or multi-tenant hosts never lend it to a neighbouring address; 19 addresses carry the contract signal only through their host and are listed with the source contract IDs.

Probed on 2026-10-16 with curl and no credentials: 38 of 50 FHIR API base addresses returned a FHIR Bundle to a Practitioner search, and 117 of 138 bulk files returned their index. 8 of the addresses that answered sit on QA or UAT hosts (9 probed). Per-address results are in detail.payer_directory_classification.probe.

The count is a floor. 279 FHIR REST endpoints in this release share the name 'FHIR API' and carry no managingOrganization, which marks one CMS collection batch; 86 of them match neither signal, and many of those look like payer directories. Payer name matching is not used to classify: it matches provider EHR servers whose names resemble payers'.

Linkage, both sides: 0 directory addresses name a payer organization as managingOrganization, 0 are listed in a payer organization's endpoint list, and 0 in an InsurancePlan's. 0 are linked to any organization at all. 30 endpoint links run from provider-typed records that carry a payer's exact name; they are listed in detail.payer_directory_classification.linkage and are mostly authenticated member APIs or EHR servers, not directories.

The control directory Capital BlueCross (https://providerdirectory-api.capbluecross.com/r4) answered 200 to an unauthenticated request and is not in the index at that address; the same payer's directory is, at https://api.capitalbluecrossfhir.com/r4/public-ma/.

Correction (2026-10-16, FHI-71): The 2026-10-14 finding counted 50 of 111,259 FHIR REST endpoints as provider-directory addresses. That counted only addresses whose URL names a directory, so it was a floor. Classified by the host as well (CMS contract IDs from the release's own InsurancePlan resources, and payer directory hosts checked by hand), the 2026-10-07 release carries at least 194: 25 by path only, 144 by host only, 25 by both. By URL shape, 138 are CMS Medicare Advantage bulk directory files, 50 are FHIR API base addresses and 6 are templates with the placeholder unfilled. Probed on 2026-10-16 with curl and no credentials, 38 of the 50 FHIR API base addresses returned a FHIR Bundle to a Practitioner search and 117 of the 138 bulk files returned their index; 9 addresses, 8 of which answered, sit on QA or UAT hosts. None of the 194 is linked to a payer organization or health plan from either side. The count is still a floor: 86 more addresses in the same CMS batch match neither signal, and many of them look like payer directories.

Reproduce with analysis/h49_recheck_release.py --dir <release dir> --release <date>.

Release watch, payer PIN: 0 of the 997 organizations typed 'pay' carry an identifier of any kind, and 0 carry a Payer Identification Number (an identifier whose type.coding has code PAYERID, from http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v2-0203). The PIN slice is in the HL7 NDH STU2 draft (Jira FHIR-57606) and not in the published STU1 (https://hl7.org/fhir/us/ndh/STU1/), so its absence is not a conformance gap against the current standard. It is watched so the first release that carries it is reported when that release is measured. The match walks identifier[].type.coding[].code under any system in the raw resource JSON; no flattened column is read. The denominator is the positive control: 997 payer-typed organizations were found, so these counts come from a query that could see them.
